text:
Morgan: Quick brain-dump — thinking about adding an eviction-proof token to prefix handoffs so a node can prove it still 'owns' a prefix briefly after losing the lease. This would buy a short grace window for in-flight requests without global coordination. Thoughts?
Jia: hmm, interesting. are you picturing the proof as signed/by-lease-epoch or just a monotonically increasing token? :thinking:
Kai: signed by epoch seems safer. otherwise we get races where new owner fast-hands and old node still serves stale reads.
Emily: If we do signed epoch tokens we need to consider key rotation/clock skew. Also how long is the grace window? 50ms? 500ms?
Morgan: yeah signed-by-epoch + nonce. idea: owner increments epoch on handoff; old owner keeps a short-lived "eviction-proof" with expiry = now + grace_ms. New owner only accepts requests if proof expired or it sees an epoch >= its own.
Jia: that matches my mental model. Concern: double-serving during overlap. We should ensure idempotency on mutation paths. Read-only is simpler.
Kai: double-serve on write is bad. propose: for write path check proof and if proof exists reject write with 409 so caller retries to new owner. That keeps reads cheap.
Emily: 409 means more retry load on control plane though. we could instead forward the write to new owner during overlap. forwards add latency but keep correctness. tradeoff.
Morgan: forwarding seems heavy at scale. maybe conditional: small writes forwarded, big ones 409. but then we complicate client semantics.
Jia: alternative: use two-phase handoff. new owner first announces intended epoch, waits grace_ms, then takes full ownership. old owner serves until expiry. This avoids signed proofs but needs a stable announce channel.
Kai: announce channel = metadata service (etcd). downside: coordination latency + failure modes if announce lost. Signed proofs are more resilient to partial failures.
Emily: operational: we should measure frequency of handoffs + typical inflight per-prefix. if handoffs are rare and inflight small, a simple announce with 200ms wait is fine. if hot-prefix churn is high, need minimal path.
Morgan: ok action plan draft: 1) prototype signed-epoch eviction-proof with grace_ms=200, proof attached to served responses for reads and checked on write path; 2) instrument handoff rate, inflight counts, and failed-write 409 rate. 3) run small canary with forward-to-new-owner disabled first.
Jia: +1. add a metric for proof-validation latency and proof-store size.
Kai: add a safety toggle to revert to strict handoff (announce+wait) if correctness anomalies detected.
Emily: I'll sketch the proto and a smoke test matrix. include cases: rapid handoff, node crash during grace, lease flapping.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: prefix-eviction-proof-prototype -> canary cluster at 2025-09-10T14:00Z (ticket #INF-2437)
Morgan: perfect. I'll write the design note with small pseudocode. quick draft:```
// on handoff (old owner): proof = sign(epoch, prefix, nonce, expiry) store proof in local cache until expiry
// on serve (old owner): attach proof header to response
// on new owner receive write: if proof present and validate(proof) -> if proof.expiry > now -> reject(409) else accept
```
Morgan: keeping it light for first pass. we'll iterate. thanks all :thumbsup:
